Who We Are

Anglers Who Borrow Check

The Rusty Hook Coding Club brings together Rust enthusiasts who share a love of the language's reliability and the quiet discipline of trout fishing. Both pursuits reward patience, precision, and a healthy respect for dangerous edges.

We meet weekly — laptops open, waders optional — to hack on Rust projects, share war stories about the borrow checker, and swap fishing spots with the same jealous secrecy we guard our async runtimes.

"Rust's ownership model is like catch-and-release: you hold it just long enough to do what you need, then let it go."

Whether you're writing your first fn main() or deep into zero-cost abstractions, there's a seat at the campfire for you.

Somewhere between lifetimes and the hatch

Why Rust?

Safe as a Barbless Hook

Rust is the fishing rod of systems languages: precise, powerful, and unforgiving of bad technique. The compiler enforces discipline so your programs don't crash in production — or disturb the fish.

Some things we love about it:

  • Memory safety without garbage collection
  • Fearless concurrency — like fishing with multiple lines
  • Zero-cost abstractions
  • The best error messages in any language
  • A community as welcoming as a warm stretch of river

Our club works on real projects: CLI tools, embedded systems, game prototypes, web servers with Axum, and the occasional silly program to calculate optimal fly patterns based on hatch data.

// The Rusty Hook — Trout Tracker

use std::collections::HashMap;

struct Catch {
    species: String,
    length_cm: f64,
    released: bool,
}

fn log_catch(
    log: &mut HashMap<String, Vec<Catch>>,
    angler: &str,
    catch: Catch,
) {
    log.entry(angler.to_string())
       .or_insert_with(Vec::new)
       .push(catch);
}

fn main() {
    let mut log = HashMap::new();

    log_catch(&mut log, "Ada", Catch {
        species: "Brown Trout".into(),
        length_cm: 42.5,
        released: true,
    });

    println!("🐟 {} catches logged.",
        log.values().map(|v| v.len())
           .sum::<usize>());
}
